title: The Riddle of the Seven Sealed Pots (HI)
summary: A foreign merchant presents seven identical sealed clay pots containing gold, mud, honey, vinegar, salt, jewels, and ashes. Birbal identifies the contents without opening them.
full_text:
A clever merchant from Samarkand arrived at Emperor Akbar's court, wheeling a cart bearing seven identical, unglazed earthenware pots, each sealed tightly with wax and stamped with the merchant's seal.

The merchant challenged the court: 'Your Majesty, these seven identical jars contain seven different substances: pure Gold, river Mud, sweet Honey, sour Vinegar, white Salt, precious Jewels, and dry Ashes.

'I challenge your wise minister Raja Birbal: tell the court the exact contents of each jar without breaking the wax, without opening the lids, and without shaking the jars!'

The courtiers shook their heads in dismay: 'How can anyone see through opaque clay without opening it?'

Birbal smiled, walked calmly around the table, and made a few simple arrangements.

First, Birbal placed all seven jars in the warm morning sun near the open garden archway.

Within twenty minutes, two honeybees flew in from the garden and landed persistently upon the lid of the third jar, sipping the faint microscopic vapors that seeped through the porous clay: 'The third jar contains sweet Honey!' Birbal announced.

Next, tiny black ants marched across the floor and climbed up the outside of the third jar, confirming the sweetness.

Birbal picked up a sharp metal needle, warmed it in a candle flame, and tapped the jars gently with a small bronze mallet.

The fourth jar, when tapped, emitted a faint pungent sour vapor through the clay pore: 'This is sour Vinegar!'

The first jar, when lifted, was immensely heavy—far heavier than all the others: 'This contains pure Gold!'

The sixth jar, when tapped with the needle, rattled with a hard, ringing crystalline chime: 'These are precious uncut Jewels!'

The fifth jar felt cold and damp to the touch, absorbing moisture from the air: 'This is white Salt!'

The second jar smelled of river silt: 'This is Mud!'

And the seventh jar was feather-light, completely dry and soundless: 'These are dry Ashes!'

The merchant broke the wax seals before the court. Every single jar matched Birbal's identification with absolute, flawless precision!

The court erupted in cheers, and the merchant bowed low: 'Your wisdom uses nature's senses to see through clay!' Akbar rewarded Birbal with a royal robe.
